# 多用户与管理后台

v2.0.0 起，Tunnel Manager 支持多用户注册与管理后台。所有数据存储在 SQLite（`data/tunnel-manager.db`，默认）或 PostgreSQL（设置 `DATABASE_URL`），换库不影响多用户与权限模型；旧版 `config.json` 会在首次启动时自动导入：原管理员账号、OAuth 连接与监控项全部继承，原文件保留作备份。

## 注册策略（管理后台 → 系统设置）

| 开关 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| 开放注册 | 关闭后登录页不再显示注册入口 |
| 注册邮箱验证 | 需要先配置 SMTP；开启后注册需填写邮箱验证码 |
| 邀请码 | 关闭 / 选填 / 必填 三种模式，邀请码可绑定用户组 |

组合效果：

- 未配置邮件服务且邀请码关闭：填写邮箱密码即可直接注册
- 配置了邮件服务：注册需要邮箱验证码（验证码 10 分钟有效，60 秒内不可重发）
- 邀请码必填：还需填写有效的邀请码

## OIDC 登录（管理后台 → OIDC 认证）

v2.9.0 的 OIDC 登录和账户绑定在 Web 端提供。Android 原生 App 尚无 OIDC 入口；仅有 OIDC 身份的用户可先在 Web 账户页设置本站密码，再通过 App 密码登录。

管理员可以添加多个标准 OIDC 接入方。配置显示名称、Issuer URL、Client ID、Client Secret、回调地址、Scopes、启用状态和排序。Issuer 用于 Discovery 自动发现端点；Scopes 默认 `openid profile email`。客户端密钥加密保存，后台读取时只返回是否已设置。

回调地址默认为当前站点的 `/api/auth/oidc/callback`。将完整地址登记到身份提供方，并确保发起登录和回调使用相同的站点域名。生产环境使用 HTTPS，本机验证允许 `localhost`、`127.0.0.1` 或 `::1` 的 HTTP 地址。

- 登录页显示已启用的接入方；首次登录按邮箱查找本站账号。
- 已有账号：接入方确认邮箱已验证时自动关联并登录；否则先发送本站邮箱验证码确认归属。未配置邮件服务时无法关联未经验证的邮箱。
- 没有账号：自动创建普通用户并分配默认用户组，独立于密码注册开关和邀请码。本站已配置 SMTP 且启用注册邮箱验证时，即使接入方已验证邮箱，也须先完成本站邮件验证。
- 关联后按接入方、Issuer 和 Subject 识别账号，外部邮箱变化不会迁移到其他账号。本站禁用状态、权限和二步验证继续生效。
- 「账户设置 → OIDC 登录账户」支持绑定、解绑；新增绑定需要确认本站密码。没有本站密码的账号可重新通过已绑定身份认证后设置密码，再使用要求密码确认的安全操作。解绑须保留密码、通行密钥或另一个已启用的 OIDC 登录方式。

已有账号关联的接入方不能更换 Issuer 或 Client ID，也不能直接删除；可先停用，再由用户解绑。修改接入方配置会使正在进行的登录失效，用户需重新发起。

## 用户与用户组

- 每个用户拥有独立的 Cloudflare 授权连接、隧道选择与监控项目，互相不可见
- 未绑定自己 Cloudflare 授权的用户无法查看或操作任何隧道/域名/DNS/监控，需先在「账户设置 → Cloudflare 授权」完成授权；未授权用户不会回退使用管理员的静态凭据
- 用户组决定权限：隧道管理、域名绑定、DNS 记录、服务监控、Cloudflare 授权
- 「默认用户组」为内置组，决定注册用户的初始权限；管理员不受权限限制
- 管理员可禁用、删除用户（重置密码会使该用户所有会话失效）

## 邀请码

在管理后台生成，可绑定用户组、限制使用次数与有效期。邀请码只在注册真正成功后才会计数，失败的注册不会消耗次数。

## 个人主页

左侧「账户设置」页的「个人主页」卡片管理当前账号的展示信息：

- **自定义名称**：展示用的昵称，不用于登录
- **头像**：本地上传（png / jpg / gif / webp，最大 4 MiB）或填写图片链接；上传后自动保存到账户
- **账户邮箱**：未绑定时可直接绑定，已绑定可修改为新邮箱；两种操作都需要当前密码确认。绑定不向新邮箱发送验证邮件，密码确认通过后直接生效。邮箱用于接收注册 / 重置验证码与通知

## 用户通知

每个用户可在左侧「通知」页面独立配置自己的提醒（与面板管理员的 Telegram 机器人无关，完全隔离）：

- **渠道**：关闭 / 仅邮箱 / 仅 Telegram / 邮箱 + Telegram
- **邮箱**：每行一个，支持多个收件人（通过全局 SMTP 发送）
- **Telegram**：填写自己的 Bot Token 与 Chat ID，由面板直接调用你的 Bot 发送
- **事件**：目前支持「登录通知」——每次账户登录成功后发送提醒（含时间与 IP），可随时关闭

保存后可点击「发送测试通知」验证配置是否生效。Telegram Token 通过 `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` 加密存储。

## Telegram 远程控制

左侧「TG 机器人」页面开放给所有登录用户，每个用户拥有**自己的 Bot**，互相完全隔离：

- 在 Telegram 与 @BotFather 创建自己的 Bot 并填写 Token，与 @userinfobot 对话获取自己的数字 TG ID
- 「授权 TG ID」填入允许向该 Bot 发送指令的 TG 账号（可多个，逗号分隔）
- 启用后 Bot 以长轮询或 Webhook 运行（见 [TG 机器人设置](/guide/telegram-bot#运行模式)），只能操作**该用户自己的账户资源**：隧道选择、转发地址、DNS 记录、域名绑定、Cloudflare 区域
- 通知与远程控制可各用各的 Bot；某一侧未配置时，页面会出现「一键复用」按钮，可直接把另一侧已配置的 Bot Token 复制过来
- **API 端点**：面板级配置（管理员在「TG 机器人」页设置），所有用户的 Bot 与通知都走该端点；国内网络建议配置自建反代，默认官方 `api.telegram.org` 国内无法直连
- 指令与原来的管理员 Bot 一致（`/help` 查看），但作用域限定在本人账户
- 管理员历史全局 Bot 配置会自动迁移为管理员的个人 Bot，无需重新配置

每个用户 Bot 的 Token 同样通过 `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` 加密存储。

## 忘记密码

- 配置了 SMTP：登录页「忘记密码？」通过注册邮箱接收重置验证码，自助完成重置
- 未配置 SMTP：请联系管理员在管理后台重置；管理员本人可使用命令行 `./tunnel-manager -set-password 新密码`

# Multi-user & admin console

Since v2.0.0 Tunnel Manager supports user registration and an admin console. Everything is stored in SQLite (`data/tunnel-manager.db` by default) or PostgreSQL (set `DATABASE_URL`), and switching backends leaves the multi-user and permission model untouched; a legacy `config.json` is imported automatically on first start — the original administrator account, OAuth connection and monitors all carry over, and the old file is kept as a backup.

## Registration policy (Admin console → System settings)

| Switch | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Open registration | Turn it off and the login page stops offering sign-up |
| Email verification | Requires SMTP first; when on, registration asks for a code sent by email |
| Invite codes | Off / optional / required, and a code can be tied to a user group |

How they combine:

- No mail service and invite codes off: an email address and a password are enough to register
- Mail service configured: registration requires the emailed code (valid for 10 minutes, no resend within 60 seconds)
- Invite codes required: a valid code is needed as well

## OIDC sign-in (Admin console → OIDC authentication)

In v2.9.0, OIDC sign-in and identity linking are available on Web. The native Android app has no OIDC entry yet; users with only an OIDC identity can set a local password in the Web account page, then sign in to the app with that password.

Administrators can add multiple standard OIDC providers with a display name, Issuer URL, Client ID, Client Secret, callback URL, scopes, enabled state and order. Discovery reads the endpoints from the issuer. Scopes default to `openid profile email`. Secrets are encrypted at rest; the console only reports whether a secret is configured.

The callback defaults to `/api/auth/oidc/callback` on the current site. Register the exact URL with the provider and use the same site hostname for starting sign-in and returning to the callback. Use HTTPS in production. HTTP is allowed for local testing on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1`.

- Enabled providers appear on the sign-in page. The first sign-in matches a local account by email.
- Existing account: a provider-verified email links the identity and signs in. Otherwise a local email code must prove ownership. Without SMTP, unverified email addresses cannot link existing accounts.
- New account: automatically creates an ordinary user in the default group, independently of password registration and invite codes. When SMTP and local registration email verification are enabled, the local email code is required even if the provider already verified the address.
- Subsequent sign-ins resolve the provider, issuer and subject. An external email change cannot move the identity to another account. Local account restrictions, permissions and two-factor authentication still apply.
- Account settings supports linking and unlinking identities. Adding a binding requires confirmation of the current local password. Accounts without a local password can reauthenticate with their linked identity to set their first password and use existing password-confirmed security settings. Unlinking must leave a password, passkey or another enabled OIDC identity available.

Providers with linked accounts cannot change their Issuer or Client ID or be deleted directly. Disable them first and have users unlink their identities. Configuration changes invalidate sign-ins already in progress.

## Users and groups

- Every user has their own Cloudflare authorization, tunnel selection and monitors; none of it is visible to anyone else
- A user who has not authorized their own Cloudflare account cannot see or touch any tunnel, domain, DNS record or monitor — they need to finish authorization under "Account settings → Cloudflare authorization" first. Unauthorized users never fall back to the administrator's static credentials
- Groups carry the permissions: tunnels, domain binding, DNS records, service monitoring, Cloudflare authorization
- The built-in "default group" decides what a newly registered user can do; the administrator is not restricted by permissions
- Administrators can disable or delete users (resetting a password invalidates all of that user's sessions)

## Invite codes

Generated in the admin console, optionally tied to a group, with a usage limit and an expiry. A code is only counted once a registration actually succeeds — failed attempts do not consume it.

## Personal profile

The "Profile" card on the "Account settings" page manages how the current account presents itself:

- **Display name**: a nickname for display only, never used to sign in
- **Avatar**: upload a local file (png / jpg / gif / webp, up to 4 MiB) or point at an image URL; uploads are saved to the account automatically
- **Account email**: bind one if there is none, or change an existing one. Both need the current password for confirmation, and no verification mail is sent to the new address — it takes effect as soon as the password check passes. The address receives registration and reset codes plus notifications

## User notifications

Each user configures their own alerts on the "Notifications" page, entirely separate from the panel administrator's Telegram bot:

- **Channels**: off / email only / Telegram only / email + Telegram
- **Email**: one address per line, several recipients allowed (sent through the global SMTP settings)
- **Telegram**: your own bot token and chat ID — the panel calls your bot directly
- **Events**: currently "login notification", sent after every successful sign-in with the time and IP, and switchable at any time

Save, then use "Send a test notification" to confirm it works. Telegram tokens are encrypted at rest with `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.

## Telegram remote control

The "TG bot" page is open to every signed-in user, and each user runs **their own bot** in complete isolation:

- Create a bot with @BotFather in Telegram and paste its token; talk to @userinfobot to learn your numeric Telegram ID
- "Authorized TG IDs" lists the Telegram accounts allowed to command that bot (several, comma-separated)
- Once enabled the bot runs by long polling or webhook (see [TG bot settings](/en/guide/telegram-bot#operating-modes)) and can only touch **that user's own resources**: tunnel selection, forwarding address, DNS records, domain bindings, Cloudflare zones
- Notifications and remote control may use different bots; when only one side is configured, a "reuse" button appears to copy the token across
- **API endpoint**: a panel-wide setting (administrators configure it on the "TG bot" page) used by every user's bot and notification. Mainland China networks generally need a self-hosted reverse proxy, since the official `api.telegram.org` is not directly reachable there
- The commands match the old administrator bot (`/help` lists them), scoped to your own account
- An administrator's previous global bot configuration is migrated to their personal bot automatically

Each user's bot token is likewise encrypted with `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.

## Forgotten passwords

- With SMTP configured: "Forgot password?" on the login page emails a reset code to the registered address for self-service recovery
- Without SMTP: ask an administrator to reset it in the admin console; the administrator themselves can use `./tunnel-manager -set-password NEW_PASSWORD` on the command line
